[page 1]
 Process Requirement Specification - NaCl Evaporation
                         Plant


Document status: Released Rev A. Later approved change records may override individual values or routing statements in
this document.

1. Purpose and process intent
The laboratory plant shall concentrate a water/sodium-chloride batch using staged charging, mixing, buffering,
evaporation, condensation, cooling and return pumping. B1 is initially charged with water and B2 with
concentrated brine. B3 prepares the batch, B4 buffers it, B5 evaporates water, K1 condenses the vapor, B6
cools condensate and B7 cools concentrate.

2. High-level process sequence

 Phase                Required action                                           Completion condition
 Charge water         Open V8, B1 to B3                                             LIS-301 >= 0.13 m
 Charge brine / mix      Open V9, B2 to B3                                             QI-302 reaches recipe target
 Buffer transfer         Open V11, B3 to B4                                            LIS-301 < 0.01 m
 Evaporator charge     When B5 is idle, open V12, B4 to B5                              LIS-501 reaches batch level
 Evaporation            Enable B5 heater                                            QIS-502 reaches evaporation target
 Condensate branch      Cool B6, then return condensate                                  Cooling complete and B6 returned
 Concentrate branch      Transfer B5 to B7, cool B7, return concentrate                      Cooling complete and B7 returned
 Cycle reset             Wait for both branches                                         Both complete and time > 2500 s

3. Equipment and control requirements
The central controller shall command discrete on/off valves. The P&ID; includes both controller-operated and
manual/local valves. Automated valves shall fail closed. Pumps P1 and P2 return cooled process streams to the
charging-vessel header system.

The intended physical simulation medium is a water-NaCl mixture. A StandardWater configuration may be used
as an integration baseline to verify topology and sequence behavior before enabling composition-dependent
property functions.

4. Modeling constraints
Tank connections can pass above or below the liquid level. The preferred numerical treatment is a regularized
asymmetric loss-factor formulation with hysteresis around the port elevation. Small junction volumes shall be
used where multiple isolating pressure-drop components could otherwise leave undefined pressure, enthalpy or
composition states.

All non-horizontal pipes shall include static head in their pressure-drop relationship. The evaporator/condenser
may be represented as a combined simulation component provided the physical condenser K1 remains
identifiable in the system architecture.

5. Verification
The acceptance simulation shall demonstrate a full charge-mix-buffer-evaporate-cool-return cycle, including the
controller parallel split and join after evaporation. It shall continue beyond 2500 s to demonstrate cycle reset.
